post_title: What will the EIA report as the week-over-week change in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories (excluding SPR) for the week ending 6 November 2026?

question.title: What will the EIA report as the week-over-week change in U.S. commercial crude oil inventories (excluding SPR) for the week ending 6 November 2026?
question.description:
U.S. commercial crude oil inventories are published every week in the EIA's [Weekly Petroleum Status Report](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/), normally on Wednesdays at 10:30 a.m. ET. Because of the Veterans Day holiday on 11 November 2026, the report covering the week ending Friday 6 November 2026 is scheduled for Thursday 12 November 2026 at 12:00 p.m. ET (17:00 UTC), per EIA's [release schedule](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php). The preceding report, covering the week ending 30 October 2026, is scheduled for 4 November 2026, so forecasters will already know that week's stock level when forecasting the 6 November figure.

In the most recent release (week ending 23 October 2026), commercial crude stocks excluding SPR were 410.6 million barrels, down 1.9 million barrels on the week and a fourth consecutive weekly decline, after 424.1 million on 2 October and 412.5 million on 16 October ([EIA weekly ending-stocks series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=WCESTUS1&f=W)). That week, Cushing stocks fell 0.6 million barrels, refinery utilisation was 92.8%, crude runs fell 123,000 barrels per day, gasoline stocks rose 3.9 million barrels, distillates fell 1.5 million barrels and net crude imports dropped 796,000 b/d ([Reuters via BOE Report](https://boereport.com/2026/10/28/us-crude-stocks-and-distillate-inventories-fall-gasoline-stocks-rise-the-eia-says/amp/)).

Weekly changes are volatile, driven by crude runs, waterborne and Canadian imports, U.S. exports, SPR transactions and weather disruptions, and recent weeks have seen swings of several million barrels. Crude prices have been elevated by Middle East escalation: Brent traded near $115/bbl and WTI near $101/bbl in late October 2026 after a reported Houthi missile strike on a Saudi refinery, with prices whipsawing on peace-talk headlines ([Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/oil-price-today-brent-crude-holds-firm-at-115-per-barrel-wti-trades-at-100/articleshow/135249292.cms)). The American Petroleum Institute publishes its own weekly inventory estimate on the Tuesday evening before the EIA release (10 November 2026 for this week); it is a useful but imperfect guide, since the two series frequently diverge by more than a million barrels.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the "Week-on-week change for United States" figure for commercial crude oil stocks (excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve) reported in the EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending 6 November 2026, scheduled for publication at 12:00 p.m. ET (17:00 UTC) on 12 November 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/. The answer is that figure in thousand barrels, with a draw reported as a negative number: for example, the −1,892 thousand barrels reported for the week ending 23 October 2026 resolves as −1892. If EIA's release for that week is delayed, the question resolves once the figure is published. Should the WPSR page no longer display that week, the figure may be taken as the week-ending stock level for 6 November 2026 minus that for 30 October 2026 from EIA's weekly ending-stocks series (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=WCESTUS1&f=W).
question.fine_print: The resolving figure is the one published in the 12 November 2026 release; later revisions to either week's stock level do not change the resolution.
